guardian.title: At least 44 dead after overcrowded ferry capsizes on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe
guardian.description:
Operation under way to rescue dozens missing after boat overturned by waves at world’s largest human-made lake

At least 44 people have died after an overcrowded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe, police said.

The boat had a capacity of 90 people, but was carrying 114 adult passengers, five crew members and an unknown number of children, Zimbabwe’s civil protection unit (CPU) said earlier on Wednesday, citing ticket sales.

guardian.description:
South African scientist’s breakthrough research shows soil fungus could be used in fight against devastating crop pest

Hearing about fields full of dead caterpillars enveloped in a mysterious white substance intrigued the South African scientist Letodi Luki Mathulwe. Something was killing off the African armyworm – one of the most devastating pests for farmers in east and southern Africa.

guardian.title: Spain to introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy
guardian.description:
Move comes in response to Rome imposing similar measures after mass migration rush to Ceuta

Spain has announced it will introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass rush of people from Morocco into Ceuta.

The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy, will start at midnight on Saturday and last until 7 September, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement.

guardian.description:
Cases have passed 4,000 and health watchdog plans to go door to door to find patients in major response escalation

The virus causing a massive outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo could be mutating, health officials fear, as confirmed cases pass 4,000.

Africa’s public health watchdog said the time for incremental action was over as they announced plans to scale up every aspect of the response and go “door to door” looking for patients.

guardian.description:
Quake of 7.4 magnitude collapses and severely damages buildings in several major cities, including Cali and Pereira

More than 100 people died after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, collapsing and severely damaging scores of buildings in major cities including Cali and Pereira.

guardian.description:
The Comac C919 will fly from Beijing to Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia, although experts say it could take generations for it to challenge the west’s dominance of the industry

China hopes to break into the world of commercial aviation with the first international flight of a Chinese-made passenger jet scheduled for Wednesday.

The Comac C919 will take off from Beijing capital international airport at 3pm, landing in Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia, just over two hours later.

euronews.description: Members of NATO met on Wednesday to discuss recent incursions into Polish and Romanian airspace and concluded that Russia bears "full responsibility" for the incidents.

euronews.description: After keeping it private for 18 months, British actor Lucy Davis has now revealed she has incurable cancer.

euronews.description: German officials accuse Moscow of waging a "hybrid" campaign of sabotage, espionage and disinformation against the country, which is among Ukraine's biggest military supporters in the war with Russia.

euronews.title: Rent in Spain tops €1,100 for 80 m²: these are the priciest and cheapest cities
euronews.description: Renting an 80-square-metre home in Spain costs an average of 1,131 euros a month, but regional disparities are stark: from 600 euros in Jaen to 1,610 in San Sebastian.

euronews.title: Queen’s Brian May outraged by AI version of album cover and tells UK PM Andy Burnham: ‘You must stop it now’
euronews.description: "Maybe this is the time to realise WE ACTUALLY DON'T NEED AI," Brian May declared when posting a ridiculously poor version of what AI thinks one of Queen's albums looks like. He has urged UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham to block AI "before it's too late".

euronews.title: IEA and OPEC split on global oil demand estimates as Strait of Hormuz closure drags
euronews.description: The world's two most watched oil forecasters published sharply conflicting views of 2026 on Wednesday, with the IEA deepening its call for the first annual demand decline since the pandemic while OPEC still sees consumption growing, as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz drags on.

rfi.title: Iran faces growing isolation and uncertain future amid 'dire' economic situation
rfi.description: As economic pressure mounts in Iran, RFI spoke to economist Djamchid Assadi about how this is leaving the country more isolated and strengthening the role of the Revolutionary Guards.

rfi.title: Russia threatens retaliatory seizures of EU ships amid new sanctions push
rfi.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday threatened to seize ships belonging to European countries in retaliation for plans to sell off cargo seized from Russian "shadow fleet" vessels.

rfi.title: French ambassador to CAR disciplined over misconduct allegations
rfi.description: France’s foreign ministry has launched disciplinary proceedings against its ambassador to the Central African Republic, following allegations that he repeatedly brought young women to the official residence in Bangui and had sexual relations with some of them.

rfi.title: France gripped by latest summer heatwave as drought conditions worsen
rfi.description: Scorching heat continued to spread across most of mainland France on Wednesday, as the Ministry for Ecological Transition met to take stock of the effects of a drought that has been steadily worsening since May.

rfi.title: Total solar eclipse over Spain to draw millions of viewers across Europe
rfi.description: Large parts of north and central Spain, plus smaller parts of Portugal, Greenland and Iceland, will see a total solar eclipse on Wednesday – with the phenomenon also visible in the south of France. Starting near the North Pole before tracking south, the total eclipse will last up to two minutes and 18 seconds, with the partial eclipse visible across much of Western Europe, including the United Kingdom, Belgium, Switzerland and northern Italy.

rfi.title: Hungary elects Orban critic Andras Baka as first president in new political era
rfi.description: Hungarian lawmakers on Tuesday approved former supreme court chief Andras Baka – a prominent critic of Viktor Orban who was ousted during the ex-premier's time in power – as the country's next head of state.

rfi.title: Assisted dying, social media and agriculture put France’s top court in spotlight
rfi.description: France’s Constitutional Council is facing a politically charged end to the summer, with judges due to rule on a series of high-profile laws – including those covering assisted dying, social media use by children, agriculture and public security.

rfi.title: Lebanon becomes first country in Middle East to abolish death penalty
rfi.description: Lebanon’s parliament on Tuesday abolished the death penalty, making it the first country in the Middle East to replace capital punishment with a sentence of life imprisonment with hard labour.

rfi.title: Former Syrian leader Assad sentenced to death in absentia over war crimes
rfi.description: A Syrian court on Tuesday sentenced former ruler Bashar al-Assad to death after a trial in absentia, convicting him of atrocities committed during the country's civil war. Six of his closest aides were also handed death sentences.

rfi.title: Race to find Ebola vaccine as DR Congo outbreak kills more than 2,000
rfi.description: The latest outbreak of Ebola has killed more than 2,000 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to health authorities. Meanwhile, international efforts have been stepped up to test a vaccine for the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever.

rfi.title: France and EU join international aid effort after Colombia earthquake
rfi.description: France has joined the European Union and a host of countries in offering assistance to Colombia, where volunteers and rescuers are searching for survivors following Monday's deadly earthquake.

rfi.title: May ’68 protest leader Cohn-Bendit pledges support to Glucksmann for 2027
rfi.description: Former Green MEP Daniel Cohn-Bendit, a historic figure on the French left, on Monday gave his support to Raphaël Glucksmann for France’s 2027 presidential election, in an interview with Le Point magazine.

rfi.title: Rebel forces in Ethiopia's Tigray state condemn army drone strikes
rfi.description: Rebel authorities on Tuesday accused the Ethiopian government of carrying out deadly drone strikes in southern Tigray state and condemned the move as "a serious escalation", amid fears of a new war.

rfi.title: France introduces tough fines for unsolicited telemarketing calls
rfi.description: France has banned unsolicited telemarketing calls under a new law to protect consumers and shield vulnerable people from fraudulent commercial practices. Individuals who make illegal calls can be fined up to €75,000 per call when the new law comes into effect on Tuesday.

rfi.title: Iran says ‘Muslim Nato’ pact reflects retreat from US security umbrella
rfi.description: Tehran has played down concerns over a new mutual defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, while portraying the agreement as evidence of declining regional reliance on the United States.

rfi.title: Moscow and Damascus reach deal over Russian military bases in Syria
rfi.description: Syria said on Sunday it had reached a deal with Moscow on the fate of Russia's two bases in the country, which it once used to provide military support to ousted leader Bashar al-Assad during the Syrian civil war.

rfi.title: Record temperatures swept regions home to 900 million people in July
rfi.description: Regions home to around 900 million people experienced their hottest July on record in 2026, including areas in the Sahel, Central America, France and Spain, according to analysis of Copernicus data.

rfi.title: Ghana backs Jamaica's petition to push UK for slavery reparations
rfi.description: Jamaica and Ghana, both former British colonies subjected to the transatlantic slave trade, are presenting a united front in the drive for reparatory justice. As Kingston prepares to lodge a formal petition with King Charles III seeking to advance its claim for reparations from the United Kingdom, Ghana's president says the global movement to address the legacy of slavery has reached a "defining moment".

lemonde.title: Muhammad Abdallah Kounta et Just Kwaou-Mathey rapportent deux médailles d’argent à la France aux championnats d’Europe d’athlétisme

lemonde.title: Chez easyJet, la grève des personnels de cabine français en plein week-end du 15 août pourrait être très suivie

lemonde.title: Cinquante ans après l’adoption de la loi fondatrice pour la protection de la nature, des avancées majeures aujourd’hui attaquées
lemonde.description: Les flamants roses, le castor et de nombreux rapaces ont bénéficié du texte promulgué en juillet 1976, qui a notamment instauré un régime de protection des espèces et reconnu la sensibilité animale. Les associations dénoncent la multiplication des accrocs.

lemonde.title: « Tous ces migrants illégaux qui arrivent sur nos côtes prennent les emplois des Britanniques » : dans la station balnéaire de Jaywick, le vote pour Nigel Farage est nourri par la peur de l’étranger

france24fr.title: 🔴 Le PSG conserve la Supercoupe d'Europe après sa victoire face à Aston Villa
Le PSG conserve la Supercoupe d'Europe après sa victoire face à Aston Villa
france24fr.description: Le PSG a battu Aston Villa 2-1 mercredi à Salzbourg, remportant la Supercoupe d'Europe pour la deuxième année consécutive. Le club de la capitale, double champion d'Europe en titre, a lancé idéalement une saison où il visera le triplé en Ligue des champions.

france24fr.title: De Tunis à Dakar, la tête dans les nuages pour observer l'éclipse solaire
france24fr.description: Une partie du monde a aujourd’hui eu la tête dans les nuages…  L’éclipse a également été observée en Afrique. C'est à Tabarka, où le phénomène a été le plus marqué en Tunisie, 59,06 % du Soleil seront masqués. L’éclipse partielle a pu être observée depuis Dakar et plusieurs régions du Sénégal, avec un maximum d’occultation d’environ 37 % du disque solaire en fin de journée.

france24fr.title: En images : les photos les plus marquantes de l'éclipse solaire
france24fr.description: Une partie de l'Espagne a été plongée mercredi dans le noir en plein jour, lorsque la Lune a entièrement masqué le Soleil, sous le regard émerveillé d'une foule massée en plusieurs points du pays. Si le reste de l'Europe a dû pour sa part se contenter d'une éclipse partielle, les photos n'en sont pas moins réussies.

france24fr.title: "On se sent tout petits" : l'émotion des spectateurs après le passage de l'éclipse
france24fr.description: Des milliers de personnes ont assisté au spectacle d'une éclipse solaire quasi-totale en France, mercredi 12 août. Tous disent leur émotion après avoir assisté à ce phénomène.

france24fr.title: Eclipse : l'électricité solaire en berne, l'astro-tourisme au firmament
france24fr.description: La disparition du Soleil derrière la Lune : un spectacle fascinant aux effets économiques multiples. La baisse de temps d'ensoleillement le 12 août réduit la production d'énergie photovoltaïque dans plusieurs pays européens. L'Allemagne devrait ainsi voir les prix de gros de l'électricité plus que doubler pendant quelques instants. L'Espagne, dans la zone de totalité, sera plus affectée mais l'a anticipé et se réjouit surtout du boom de l'astrotourisme. L'Islande aussi dans une moindre mesure.

france24fr.title: Le moment de l'éclipse solaire totale en Espagne
france24fr.description: Voici le moment où la Lune a entièrement recouvert le Soleil lors d'une éclipse totale en Espagne ce mercredi.

france24fr.title: Séisme en Colombie : le secteur du cinéma se mobilise la nuit pour éclairer les décombres
france24fr.description: Armés de projecteurs habituellement utilisés en studio, des travailleurs du secteur du cinéma se mobilisent dans la ville de Cali depuis lundi, à la nuit tombée, pour éclairer les décombres et ainsi faciliter le travail de recherche des survivants. Le séisme qui a touché l’ouest de la Colombie a fait plus de 200 morts.

france24fr.title: Ebola en RDC : le cap des 2000 morts franchi
france24fr.description: En RDC, l’épidémie d’Ebola approche du bilan le plus meurtrier jamais enregistré dans le pays. Le virus a déjà fait 2 011 morts sur 4 381 cas confirmés, contre 2 300 décès lors de l’épidémie de 2018-2020. Les autorités congolaises estiment que le pic n’est pas encore atteint.

france24fr.title: LIBYE : Funérailles du chef des renseignements de Haftar tué dans un attentat
france24fr.description: 🇱🇾 En Libye, Fauzi al-Mansouri, chef des renseignements de l’Est a été tué lundi dans un attentat à la voiture piégée à Benghazi. Une attaque qui porte un coup au camp du maréchal Haftar, qui vise à étendre son contrôle sur la Libye.

france24fr.title: Éclipse solaire: quelles conséquences sur l'Environnement?
france24fr.description: L'éclipse solaire perturbe les activités de la faune, fait baisser la température et la force du vent. On passe en revue les effets de cette absence momentanée de lumière en plein jour sur l'Environnement.

france24fr.title: Éclipse : le gouvernement français avait-il distribué 35 millions de lunettes gratuites en 1999 ?
france24fr.description: Fustigeant la gestion gouvernementale de l'éclipse partielle de 2026, des personnalités politiques affirment que lors de l’éclipse solaire de 1999, le gouvernement français aurait distribué gratuitement 35 millions de paires de lunettes de protection. Si la mobilisation gouvernementale a été plus importante en 1999 qu'en 2026, plus de la moitié des lunettes avaient cependant été vendues par le secteur marchand.

france24fr.title: Rwanda : Nyakabingo, mine de tungstène stratégique pour la défense américaine.
france24fr.description: 🇷🇼 Au Rwanda, la mine de Nyakabingo est devenue en quelques mois l’un des principaux fournisseurs de tungstène des États-Unis. Ce métal stratégique, indispensable à l’industrie de défense, pourrait prendre une importance croissante alors que Washington prévoit de bannir les approvisionnements chinois destinés à ses usages militaires.

france24fr.title: Football : le PSG lance sa saison face à Aston Villa
france24fr.description: Le Paris Saint-Germain retrouve la compétition ce mercredi soir à Salzbourg, en Autriche, avec la Supercoupe d’Europe face à Aston Villa. Après une saison exceptionnelle et un deuxième sacre consécutif en Ligue des champions, les Parisiens ont l’occasion de poursuivre leur moisson de trophées face au vainqueur de la Ligue Europa. Récit de Julien Dubois.

france24fr.title: Fragilisé à la tête de la Fifa, Gianni Infantino "a de bonnes chances de passer l'été"
france24fr.description: Le président de la Fifa est dans l'œil du cyclone depuis l'annonce de son projet controversé d'ouvrir l'instance du football mondial à des investisseurs privés. Malgré un retrait rapide de ce projet, plusieurs confédérations, dont la puissante UEFA européenne, maintiennent Gianni Infantino sous pression. De quoi le pousser à la démission ? Rien n'est moins sûr d'ici la prochaine élection de la Fifa en mars prochain. Explications.

france24fr.title: Sécheresse en France : à Gérardmer, le lac bientôt pompé pour fournir l’eau potable
france24fr.description: À Gérardmer, dans les Vosges, le pompage de l’eau du lac débute ce mercredi 12 août pour alimenter le réseau d’eau potable. La baisse du niveau de la nappe phréatique ne permet plus de répondre suffisamment aux besoins des habitants et des communes voisines. Reportage France 2.

zeit.description: Karoline Leavitt brachte erst im Mai ihr zweites Kind zur Welt. Nun verlässt sie ihren Posten als Pressesprecherin des Weißen Hauses.

nzz.description: Erst vor neun Monaten hat die Sprinterin Mujinga Kambundji ihr erstes Kind geboren. Auf dem Weg zurück gibt es Aufs und Abs. Im 200-m-Halbfinal an den Europameisterschaften in Birmingham wurde sie Letzte. Und gab danach ehrlich Einblick in ihr Gefühlsleben.

nzz.description: Medizinische Versorger handeln mit Pharmafirmen Vergünstigungen aus, liefern sie aber nicht den Krankenkassen ab. Das gilt in der Branche immer noch als Kavaliersdelikt, wie ein Bericht der Finanzkontrolle zeigt.

nzz.description: Donald Trump regiert zum zweiten Mal als amerikanischer Präsident – mit weitreichenden innen- und aussenpolitischen Folgen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.description: Die Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und der Hamas ist brüchig. Bis zu einem nachhaltigen Frieden im Nahen Osten ist es ein weiter Weg. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Sonnenfinsternis über Europa: die spektakulärsten Bilder
nzz.description: An diesem Mittwochabend schiebt sich der Mond vor die Sonne. In Grönland, Island, Spanien und im Norden Portugals wird man eine totale Sonnenfinsternis beobachten können, in der Schweiz und in Deutschland eine partielle. So erleben die Menschen das Ereignis.

nzz.title: ORF in der Krise: Sparzwang und Millionenklage des Ex-Chefs
nzz.description: Wegen geplanter Kürzungsmassnahmen erwägt Österreichs öffentlichrechtlicher Sender eine Verfassungsbeschwerde gegen die Regierung. Derweil klagt der nach Vorwürfen der sexuellen Belästigung entlassene ehemalige Generaldirektor Roland Weissmann gegen seine Kündigung.

nzz.title: Nur mit 6 Millionen Franken, aber mit der «Grande Dame der Teilchenphysik»: So will Rösti den Gipfel zur künstlichen Intelligenz in Genf zum Erfolg machen
nzz.description: Im Juni 2027 findet in Genf der grösste KI-Gipfel statt. Da der Bund sparen muss, dürften aber nur wenige Staatschefs anreisen.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Migrationskrise in Europa: Marokko warnt vor erneutem Migrationssturm nach Ceuta

nzz.description: Wie wirken sich Energiewende und globale Krisen auf Strom- und Gaspreise aus? Hier gibt es jeden Tag die aktuellen Zahlen.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

nzz.title: Die Inflation in Deutschland ist zurück – und könnte bald ordentlich zulegen
nzz.description: Im Juli haben vor allem die Preise für Energie deutlich angezogen. Neben dem Krieg im Nahen Osten bedroht die Trockenheit die Stabilität.

spiegel.title: Mord an Rob und Michele Reiner: Sohn Nick soll seinen Eltern aufgelauert haben
spiegel.description: Der Sohn des Hollywoodpaars Rob und Michele Reiner steht wegen Mordes an seinen Eltern vor Gericht. Eine Anklageschrift legt nun neue Vorwürfe gegen den 32-Jährigen offen.

spiegel.title: Fußball: Spanier Xavi Hernández wird neuer Trainer der Niederländer
spiegel.description: Die Fußballauswahl der Niederlande hat einen neuen Trainer. Der frühere Barcelona-Star Xavi Hernández soll das Team bis zur Weltmeisterschaft 2030 coachen. Erster Gegner: die deutsche Mannschaft.

spiegel.title: Karoline Leavitt: Trumps Pressesprecherin gibt Posten im Weißen Haus auf
spiegel.description: Seit Beginn von Donald Trumps zweiter Amtszeit war Karoline Leavitt Pressesprecherin des Weißen Hauses und eine seiner größten Unterstützerinnen. Nun zieht sie sich abrupt zurück. Aus familiären Gründen, wie es heißt.

spiegel.title: Sonnenfinsternis: So erlebten Millionen Menschen das Himmelsereignis
spiegel.description: Millionen Menschen quer durch Europa starrten in den Himmel – und wurden nicht enttäuscht. Das Spektakel am Himmel lieferte faszinierede Bilder, die besten im Video.

spiegel.title: Schwimm-EM in Paris: Johannes Liebmann holt Gold mit Europarekord über 800 Meter
spiegel.description: Schneller war noch kein Europäer über diese Distanz: Nachwuchsstar Johannes Liebmann gewann in Paris über 800 Meter Freistil. Und das vor seinem eigenen Teamkollegen Sven Schwarz.

spiegel.title: WHO kritisiert Donald Trumps Dekret zu Kinderimpfungen scharf
spiegel.description: Die US-Regierung erkennt nur noch Impfungen gegen elf Krankheiten als Empfehlungen für alle Kinder an. Die Weltgesundheitsorganisation wirft dem Präsidenten nun vor, gegen die Erkenntnisse der Wissenschaft zu handeln.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: Bündnispläne bei AfD-Sieg - Was wirklich hinter Sahra Wagenknechts Taktik steckt
spiegel.description: Bei der Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt droht nach dem möglichen Erfolg der AfD Koalitionschaos: Sahra Wagenknecht wittert ihre Chance und will als Königsmacherin auftreten. Kann das gelingen?

spiegel.title: Sonnenfinsternis: Die schönsten Bilder des Abends
spiegel.description: Zuerst schiebt sich der Mond vor den rechten unteren Rand der Sonnenscheibe, dann bildet sich eine Sichel. Tausende verfolgen in Europa die Sonnenfinsternis. Die Bilder des Himmelsspektakels.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump wegen Premium-Zugangs zu Truth Social verklagt
spiegel.description: Für Zehntausende Dollar im Monat die Social-Posts des US-Präsidenten früher sehen als andere: Dieses Premiumangebot von Donald Trumps Truth Social sei »korrupt und verfassungswidrig«, sagen Medienorganisationen.

spiegel.title: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern: Streit um Ausladung von CDU und Linken aus TV-Runde
spiegel.description: Die Spitzenkandidaten der CDU und der Linken in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern sind zu einer Fernsehdebatte erst ein-, dann wieder ausgeladen worden. Beide geben nun Ministerpräsidentin Manuela Schwesig die Schuld.

spiegel.title: Eurovision Song Contest: Ausrichter kann Siegerländer als Gastgeber ausschließen
spiegel.description: Wer den Eurovision Song Contest gewinnt, darf im nächsten Jahr die große Party zu sich ins Land holen. Mit einer neuen Regelung hält der Ausrichter es sich ab sofort offen, bestimmte Länder als Gastgeber auszuschließen.

spiegel.title: Rechtsextremismus: Kinderzimmer-Nazis – immer jünger, immer radikaler - SPIEGEL TV
spiegel.description: Versuchter Mord, gefährliche Brandstiftung, Mitgliedschaft in einer terroristischen Vereinigung. Der jüngste Täter der rechtsextremen Gruppe »Letzte Verteidigungswelle« war zum Tatzeitpunkt 14 Jahre alt. Ihre Taten filmten sie selbst.

spiegel.title: Reform der Geheimdienste: Mehr Macht für BND und Verfassungsschutz, mehr Aufsicht
spiegel.description: Es ist richtig, dass die deutschen Geheimdienste mehr Befugnisse bekommen. Die Gefahr durch Russland ist real. Doch mehr Macht erfordert auch mehr Kontrolle.

spiegel.title: Matthias Lilienthal über das »Volksbad«: »Die Duschen sind aktuell nicht funktionsfähig«
spiegel.description: Gerade eröffnete die Berliner Volksbühne ein Schwimmbad, nun muss es schon wieder vorübergehend schließen. Intendant Matthias Lilienthal über die Gründe – und seine Idee, ins »Volksbad« stundenweise nur nichtweiße Menschen zu lassen.

spiegel.title: »The End of Oak Street«: Anne Hathaway und Ewan McGregor im Dino-Chaos
spiegel.description: In »The End of Oak Street« mit Anne Hathaway und Ewan McGregor wird eine Musterfamilie aus den Achtzigerjahren in die Ära der Dinosaurier versetzt. Gruselig? Ja, aber auch so albern, dass man sich gut unterhalten fühlen kann.

spiegel.title: WNBA: »MAGA-Barbie«, Trans-Hass und »White Privilege« – wie Sophie Cunningham den US-Basketball ins Chaos stürzt
spiegel.description: Die Debatten über die US-Liga WNBA drehen sich um alles außer Basketball: Ob trans Frauen gegen Frauen spielen dürfen oder ob weiße Spielerinnen bevorzugt werden. Das Gesicht der Absurdität ist Sophie Cunningham.

spiegel.title: Rekord: Dieser Wagen mit Wasserstoffantrieb fährt mehr als 650 km/h
spiegel.description: Im US-Bundesstaat Utah stellt der »JCB Hydromax« einen Geschwindigkeitsrekord für Autos mit Wasserstoff-Verbrennungsmotor auf. Am Steuer saß Andy Green, der 1997 als erster Mensch auf vier Rädern die Schallmauer durchbrach.

spiegel.title: Sonnenfinsternis heute im Livestream: Sehen Sie, wie es plötzlich dunkel wird
spiegel.description: Die Sonnenfinsternis naht – und Sie brauchen weder eine Spezialbrille noch ein Flugticket nach Mallorca, wo das Ereignis am besten zu sehen sein wird. Sie müssen nicht mal vom Sofa aufstehen: Hier ist der Livestream.

observador.title: África do Sul quer reembolso de custos de repatriamentos
observador.description: Pretória escreveu ao Maláui, Nigéria e Etiópia a pedir compensação. Os repatriamentos custaram cinco vezes mais do que o orçamento previsto para as operações.

observador.title: Moçambique pede apoio para extensão de missão militar da UE
observador.description: Ministra moçambicana afirma que a Eslováquia "manifestou abertura" para continuar a apoiar o país. Governo interessado em expandir cooperação com a Dinamarca. Missão foi prolongada até 2028.

observador.title: JMJ Seul 2027 já tem mil jovens portugueses inscritos
observador.description: A peregrinação "Vamos Juntos à JMJ Seul 2027" ultrapassou os mil inscritos. A Conferência Episcopal Portuguesa disse que o número "traduz o desejo de jovens portugueses de começar a fazer caminho".

observador.title: Bombeiros resgatam homem após queda nas Sete Lagoas
observador.description: O homem, de 66 anos, terá sofrido uma fratura numa perna. Estabilizado no local, foi encaminhado para o Hospital de Braga. Foram mobilizadas três viaturas e dez operacionais.

observador.title: Parlamento elege quatro membros da UNITA para a CNE
observador.description: Projeto de lei aprovado por unanimidade. Decisão arrastava-se há mais de um ano, depois da UNITA recusar indicar representantes, alegando ser "ilegal" a distribuição de assentos.

observador.title: Chega/Açores quer nova Segurança Social para pescadores
observador.description: Partido irá entregar anteproposta de lei na Assembleia da República. Deputados estiveram reunidos com sindicatos para avaliar as dificuldades dos pescadores. Pedem alteração de regime.

observador.title: Angola. Dívida tem gastos 3 vezes maiores que setor social
observador.description: Encargos financeiros absorveram 56% da despesa pública entre abril e junho, crescendo 123% face a 2025. Setor social ficou-se pelos 16% do total executado.

observador.title: 22h. Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa já saiu do Hospital de Faro

observador.title: Estado exerce preferência sobre manuscritos de Pessoa
observador.description: Direito de preferência exercido num leilão da Cabral Moncada de junho inclui cartas inéditas de Pessoa a Ofélia Queiroz e o manuscrito de "O Homem Universal" de Pascoaes.

observador.title: Eclipse. Animais tranquilos no Zoológico de Lisboa

observador.title: Não deite os óculos fora. Até fim de 2027 há muitos eclipses

observador.description: A música tocou como previsto, mas durante 30 minutos, muitos olhos com óculos de papel viraram-se para o céu e para o sol, para ver um eclipse "muito incrível" e "histórico".

observador.title: Quando os galácticos se alinham, a orquestra segue igual

observador.title: Ministro de São Tomé exonerado após processo-crime

observador.title: Peregrinos viram o eclipse no Santuário de Fátima
observador.description: O próximo eclipse será só em 2144. Santuário acolhe por estes dias a tradicional Peregrinação dos Emigrantes.

observador.title: Fatoumata Diallo é medalha de bronze europeia
observador.description:
A atleta de 26 anos cumpriu a promessa que tinha feito antes da prova: queria um recorde pessoal e uma medalha. À sua frente ficaram as atletas eslovaca Emma
Zapletalová e a britânica Emily Newnham.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

phys-org.title: A dying star offers a rare glimpse of how the universe recycles its raw materials
phys-org.description: Astronomers have captured an unprecedented image of a cosmic recycling project in progress—fragments of a dying star being busted up, stripped and absorbed into interstellar space.

phys-org.title: Putting out wildfires: How peat restoration has reduced fire risk in Indonesia's tropical forests
phys-org.description: Peatland fires in Indonesia pose a major threat to habitats, wildlife and people. That risk is exacerbated by the country's periodic El Niño warming phases, which bring prolonged drought.

phys-org.title: Fast-moving wildfires may prevent western forests from recovering
phys-org.description: The severe, drought-fueled fires now burning across much of the American West and Canada may be scorching forests so thoroughly that they cannot recover to the forests they once were, new research shows. A study by Colorado State University, Western Colorado University and others found that the fastest-moving forest fires not only burn more area but also burn more severely, leaving fewer surviving trees to reseed the landscape and opening the door to different species and vegetation types.

phys-org.title: Pain isn't the point: European viper venoms may have evolved to subdue prey
phys-org.description: For many people, the fear of venomous snakes is linked to one thing: pain. Yet new research led by scientists at Bangor University suggests that, for Europe's vipers, at least, causing pain may never have been a driving force in the evolution of their venom.

phys-org.title: Greener processing cuts cost of novel material for water decontamination
phys-org.description: University of Birmingham scientists who used green chemistry to make a next-generation metal-organic framework (MOF) for capturing heavy metals from wastewater have shown that it is cheaper and more resource-efficient to produce than a similar MOF processed conventionally.

phys-org.title: Wars between nations face persistent escalation risk, decades of conflict data suggest
phys-org.description: Military leaders frequently underestimate how big the wars they engage in will get. Gen. Douglas MacArthur predicted U.S. troops could come home from the Korean War in time for Christmas, just months after the conflict started. But Chinese attacks that winter extended the war for years. And President Donald Trump said in March that the Iran war would be a "short-term excursion," but it has now lasted more than five months, with periods of escalation.

phys-org.title: Novel polymer membrane design improves high-purity hydrogen separation
phys-org.description: In Nature Communications a research team led by Professor Tae-Hyun Bae of the KAIST Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering introduced hydrogen-selective transport pathways at the angstrom scale inside polymer membranes and clarified their separation performance through the concept of "network completeness."

phys-org.description: The building blocks of rocky planets may have begun forming just 100 million years after the Big Bang—long before the first galaxies even existed—according to new research from the University of Portsmouth.

phys-org.title: Soil-dwelling myxobacteria reveal five new classes of bioactive compounds
phys-org.description: Most antibiotics used clinically are based on natural compounds produced by bacteria and other microorganisms. At the Helmholtz Institute for Pharmaceutical Research Saarland (HIPS), researchers are using soil-dwelling myxobacteria as a source of new active ingredients. They are able to discover new active compounds primarily in bacteria that have not yet been extensively studied.

phys-org.title: A $10 soil test goes global with virtual reality training for farmers
phys-org.description: Last year, we described Agrilo, an affordable "colorimetric" soil-testing system developed through research at MacEwan University. Using a smartphone camera to interpret color changes, Agrilo measures soil nutrients and can provide farmers with timely guidance to support fertilizer decisions.

phys-org.title: Europe's worst medieval flood highlights risk of successive extreme events
phys-org.description: New research involving the University of Liverpool has provided comprehensive insights into the largest flood event in Europe over the past millennium—the flood traditionally known as "St. Mary Magdalene's Flood" of 1342.

phys-org.title: DNA research highlights the genetic vulnerability of Asian elephants
phys-org.description: The DNA of Asian elephants tells a concerning story. Although all four subspecies are under pressure, there are considerable differences in their genetic health. In an article published in the journal Genome Biology and Evolution, researchers show how whole-genome analyses can help identify more precisely which populations are most vulnerable and where conservation measures could have the greatest impact.

phys-org.title: Severe weather now a key predictor of where bird species occur in North America
phys-org.description: Scorching heat waves, severe cold snaps and other extreme weather events are limiting where species can exist—and affecting biodiversity estimates—for more than 500 North American bird species, according to a new, Yale–led study. The issue is particularly acute in the Great Plains and southwestern regions of the United States, where species ranges and total species counts are significantly overestimated when variable and extreme weather are not considered, the study says.

phys-org.title: An open-source tool for automated consolidation of lipid data
phys-org.description: In collaboration with the University of Vienna, the Technical University of Munich (TUM), and Heidelberg University, researchers at the TUD Dresden University of Technology have developed an innovative tool that significantly simplifies lipid research. The new open-source platform, LipidLibrarian, enables the automated consolidation of fragmented data from international lipid databases, such as LIPID MAPS, SwissLipids, and ALEX123, into a single, user-friendly interface for the first time. phys-org.title: Sugar swap simplifies production of promising targeted cancer therapies
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Wisconsin–Madison have developed a simpler way to produce a fast-growing class of targeted cancer therapies, a discovery that could make the medicines easier to manufacture consistently while driving the development of new treatment options.

phys-org.title: Cutting traffic pollution alone could worsen Taiwan's haze
phys-org.description: Taiwan's air has gotten measurably cleaner over the past decade, yet in many towns the hazy, milky-white sky that blurs mountains and city skylines has not cleared at the same pace. A research team led by Prof. Ta-Chih Hsiao from the Graduate Institute of Environmental Engineering at National Taiwan University set out to find out why.

phys-org.title: Stellar stream beyond Milky Way offers new tool to map dark matter
phys-org.description: In the image above, a faint trail of stars can be seen stretching across the galaxy. These structures, known as globular cluster stellar streams, are coherent stellar structures that retain a record of their dynamical history and can provide unique insights into the evolution of galaxies and the nature of dark matter.

phys-org.title: Genetic switch could help tomatoes produce fruit in cold weather
phys-org.description: Every tomato begins with a flower. But before a fruit can grow, an intricate sequence of events must happen in perfect order. The flower's male and female organs must develop together, pollen must be released at exactly the right time, and fertilization must occur.

proj-syn.title: Europe Failed the Ceuta Test
proj-syn.description: The current migration crisis is eating away at the solidarity on which the European Union depends, fueling the rise of the far right and pushing leaders to adopt increasingly hardline policies. But the Ceuta debacle shows why such measures cannot address the deeper forces driving migration.

proj-syn.title: The Legacy of Zhu Rongji
proj-syn.description: Zhu Rongji’s personal history and political challenges made it highly unlikely that he would rise to the pinnacle of Chinese politics. Once there, he implemented many of the reforms that turned the country into an economic powerhouse.

proj-syn.title: The Twilight of the ICC
proj-syn.description: Born amid the euphoria of the West’s Cold War victory, the International Criminal Court embodied the aspiration that international law could transcend politics. But the ICC always represented victors’ justice, and it was never equipped to operate in a world shaped by Machtpolitik.

proj-syn.title: Will Latin America Embrace Guerrilla Geopolitics?
proj-syn.description: The resurgence of guerrilla warfare in Ukraine and Iran has underscored the potential benefits of asymmetric action in today’s increasingly multipolar world. Latin America, in particular, should consider how to leverage its many strengths to remedy its relatively weak position on the global stage.

proj-syn.title: China’s Biggest Weakness on AI
proj-syn.description: When a state can credibly promise that labor displacement will not mean destitution, workers and their representatives are more likely to accept technological change. But since China can promise no such thing, its lack of a robust welfare state has emerged as a fundamental weakness in the broader AI race.

proj-syn.title: The Monetary Roots of Political Extremism
proj-syn.description: While the global economy generates unprecedented wealth for plutocrats like Elon Musk, it is, by design, highly unequal, dangerously over-indebted, prone to recurring financial crises, and ecologically disastrous. In such a context, radical reforms will be needed, beginning with the rejection of money as a commodity.

proj-syn.title: The Return of the Power Trust
proj-syn.description: A century ago, the US power industry was dominated by sprawling, heavily indebted holding companies until their collapse forced the federal government to break them up. Now, the pattern is repeating, with mega-mergers and buyouts advancing a debt-heavy business model at the expense of households and communities.

proj-syn.title: Morocco’s Bet on Targeted AI
proj-syn.description: Rather than join the global race for computing power, Morocco has focused on building sovereignty over its data, talent, and uses of AI, because technological power will be measured by usefulness, not by domination. This strategy calls for the country to embrace innovation without ceding its identity to foreign models.

proj-syn.title: Dude, Where’s My Recession?
proj-syn.description: Despite a series of major negative shocks, some of them unprecedented, the US economy continues to grow in line with its estimated long-run potential. Yet given obvious and mounting risks, from debt-financed speculation to geopolitical tensions, the appearance of resilience should not be confused with the real thing.

proj-syn.title: The Rise of the Token Economy
proj-syn.description: Millions of people continuously generate the raw material on which AI is trained, yet almost none shares in the wealth it creates. This underscores the need for data cooperatives representing internet users, creators, and other rights holders to negotiate access to the content being fed to large language models.

proj-syn.title: Excess Savings Are Driving the New China Shock
proj-syn.description: The current China shock combines continued supply upgrading with an absorption problem: the decline in property and related investment has reduced domestic demand, but national saving remains very high. The result is a larger savings-investment surplus that spills into net exports.

proj-syn.title: The World Economy Is Swerving, and the Destination Is Unknown
proj-syn.description: The days of unfettered globalization, multilateral rule of law, commonly accepted limits on economic statecraft, and widely shared macroeconomic objectives are now long gone. A perpetual, directionless transition is our new reality, and corporate executives, investors, and policymakers must adapt accordingly.

proj-syn.title: Is China Really a Beggar-thy-Neighbor Power?
proj-syn.description: When major economies are running at near full capacity, it is not clear that trade deficits should be a cause for concern, since they represent a transfer of purchasing power from surplus countries. Under the current circumstances, then, China’s widely criticized surpluses might as well be called enrich-thy-neighbor.

proj-syn.title: No Escape from the Russian Terror Playbook
proj-syn.description: When Vladimir Putin revives Stalin-era repression tactics, he does not do so in service of some lofty ideology or grand project. Rather, he and his security apparatus are seeking to safeguard their own power indefinitely—and, as Russians well know, they will stop at nothing to succeed.

proj-syn.title: The Extractive Trap Has a Green Exit
proj-syn.description: For resource-rich developing countries, decades of resource extraction have produced income concentration, economic dependency, external vulnerabilities, and the weakening of other productive sectors. Achieving broad-based prosperity requires a new approach, one which leverages South-South cooperation to build green industries.

proj-syn.title: The Last Trump Election
proj-syn.description: No matter what US President Donald Trump says or does in response to the results of this November’s midterms, he will have faced his final popular vote. There will be further damage done to public confidence in American democratic institutions, but the institutions themselves will hold.

proj-syn.title: The Ceuta Crisis Is About More Than Migration
proj-syn.description: When tens of thousands of people recently entered the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from neighboring Morocco, European leaders lapsed into recriminations, reigniting the debate on migration. But the bigger challenge is to address a long-simmering territorial dispute between Spain and Morocco.

proj-syn.title: The Rising Price of a Cheap Renminbi
proj-syn.description: Renminbi appreciation would not, on its own, rebalance China’s economy and eliminate its massive surpluses. But by increasing households’ purchasing power over imports and compressing tradable-sector margins, it would raise the cost of avoiding reform.
